text:
Jack Drury went back to Colorado on Nov 5 alongside Ross Colton, two former Avalanche forwards now playing big minutes for a Nashville team that has not lost since Oct 31. Drury's role is the less glamorous one: more than 17 minutes a night, 24 blocked shots, penalty kill duty.

His scoring is thin, 5 points in 19 games and one goal over his last ten, and his individual chances (0.42 expected goals per 60) are lower than our numbers expected. He ranks near the bottom of the league in our wins added. But that measure is built from goals and saves, and Drury's case is made in his own end. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.26 fewer expected goals per 60 with him on the ice last season, 99th percentile among forwards, though with strong Colorado teammates around him. This season the Predators are slightly better at five on five with him than without. If you are watching him for points, you are watching the wrong thing.
headline: Jack Drury is the defensive center Nashville wanted
